clues.title: Language: swirly, unique script
text: Georgian is a Kartvelian language and the official language of Georgia. The Georgian script is overall quite swirly and unique, not resembling any other European language. On directional signs, Latin script is very commonly used alongside Georgian.

NOTE: It is possible to confuse Georgian and other swirly scripts found in Asia. Georgia should however look fairly different from these countries (like India, for example). As a former member of the Soviet Union, Georgia still has visible similarities with Russia when it comes to infrastructure and more.

images.caption: Blue road sign with Georgian script and Latin transliteration

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: A very curly script that looks like no other European language. Signs often add Latin letters next to it. Don't mix it up with Indian scripts, and expect some Russia-like infrastructure.

differs.how: Indian scripts look fairly different from this swirly script
